messages.text: There's a comment on PR #101, have a look
I’ll read the new comment on PR #101 and check it against the current changes.

The [reviewer’s comment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/101#issuecomment-6419397508) asks for a Fatras cross-check using Gaussian-smeared measurements with widths measured over all cluster sizes.

Yes, the current baseline uses cluster-size-dependent errors from the independent Fatras training sample, applied after geometric clustering. I’ll add the smeared comparison so we can check how much the geometric digitization contributes to the pull shapes.

I’ll pool all cluster sizes within each ACTS volume and measured coordinate to set the Gaussian widths, using the existing independent training sample. The Spack preflight still warns about changed setup fingerprints; I’ll verify the existing isolated runtime before running the cross-check.

The pooled widths are ready: they use all 699,273 training measurements across 52 volumes and 90 measured coordinates. The new Gaussian configuration will use those same widths for both the random shifts and fitted measurement covariance. SoftEng is preparing a native pilot to verify this.

The native Gaussian pilot is running. One detail matters for interpretation: ACTS discards smeared positions that fall outside the sensor bounds. I’ll retain those losses and check measurement residuals as well as track pulls, since Gaussian measurement errors alone don’t guarantee Gaussian track pulls.

The 100-event pilot passed: all tracks fitted, both measurement dimensions were correct, and every written measurement variance matched the frozen Gaussian width squared. The three 20,000-event Fatras samples at 1, 10, and 100 GeV are now starting at one fixed source revision.
The full samples are progressing. I’ve also recorded the reviewer’s comment and reconciled the now-closed baseline turn’s usage in its original account; this cross-check has a separate record.
All three samples have passed halfway. The comparison will show both the measurement-level Gaussian check and the track pulls, with the original geometric results alongside them.

All three samples completed. Fatras fitted 19,992, 19,998, and 19,999 tracks at 1, 10, and 100 GeV—the same counts as the geometric reference. There were no fit failures, invalid covariances, or sensor-bound losses. I’m reducing the pull distributions and measurement checks now.

The measurement residuals pass the Gaussian sanity check: their pooled widths are 1.0002, 0.9997, and 1.0000. Track-level tails remain, especially at 1 GeV. The new plots compare both digitization modes so this difference is visible; an independent review is next.

The independent reviewer caught a detail we misstated: ACTS appears to default to ten retries for out-of-bounds Gaussian draws. The runs are retained. I’m verifying that setting and correcting the report and plot labels; zero lost measurements does not prove that no draws were retried.

The pinned ACTS source confirms ten retries, allowing up to eleven draw attempts. I’ve corrected the captions and metadata annotations while preserving the original reports and simulation outputs. The numerical results are unchanged; the reviewer is checking the correction now.

The activated native runtime also reports a retry limit of ten, and all eight smearing controls pass there. The independent checks have reproduced the training widths, measurement variances, fit counts, and comparison histograms. Final figure and annotation checks are finishing.

The independent review is complete with no remaining scientific or provenance blocker. It reproduced all 42 comparison histograms and confirmed the retry correction. I’m fixing a stale test-count sentence, recording the assessment and usage, then checking the final PR head.
